name: VARoleArbiterCompetitorPricingReport

custom.system_prompt: Odalys and Ingmar, coworkers, each saw a different figure for a competitor's pricing — one from a recent report, one from an older deck. They disagree about which number is current before a client call. They ask Sigma to compare the sources.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Neutral, precise about dates and figures

sound_effects_config.prompt: Open-plan office, keyboard clicks, distant conversation

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Odalys and Ingmar disagree about a competitor's current pricing figure right before a client call — Odalys citing a number from a recent report, Ingmar recalling a different, older figure from a deck he trusts. They ask Sigma to compare the two and determine which is current. Keep every line short and professional but natural.

user2.name: Ingmar
user2.tts_prompt: Calm, cautious, wants the source checked

variations.context: Coworkers disagreeing about a competitor's current pricing figure just before a client call

setting.relationship_dynamic: Odalys moves fast on instinct and recent numbers; Ingmar double-checks by habit
setting.background: They have a client call in a few minutes and need the correct figure before it starts
setting.conversation_style: Short, quick, professional but pointed given the time pressure

scenario_template.topic: Odalys states the figure from the recent report with full confidence; Ingmar cites a different, older figure he trusts, and questions where hers came from. A few short quick exchanges under time pressure.
scenario_template.note: Neither has time to fully research mid-conversation.

scenario_template.topic: Odalys asks Sigma to quickly confirm which figure is current, addressing Sigma directly in one short line, given the time pressure.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, quick — which number is actually current?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma states which figure is current and briefly why — for example the older deck predates a recent price change. One or two short sentences, no more, given the time pressure.
scenario_template.note: Sigma keeps this fast given they're about to be on a call.

scenario_template.topic: Odalys is satisfied but doesn't dwell on it, already moving to prep; Ingmar notes plainly that his deck needs updating, a little irritated at himself rather than at her. Keep this realistic and fast, matching the time pressure.
scenario_template.mood: Quick, focused on the call ahead
scenario_template.note: No time for a drawn-out reaction given the deadline.

scenario_template.topic: They confirm they're aligned and head into the call, one short line each.

user1.name: Odalys
user1.role: Competitive, quick sales strategist who cites figures readily and moves fast. Speaks in short sentences. Accepts correction efficiently under time pressure rather than dwelling on it.

user2.name: Ingmar
user2.role: Calm, cautious account manager who double-checks numbers by habit. Speaks in short sentences. Mildly irritated at his own outdated source rather than at his colleague.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Arbiter. Quickly resolves which of two conflicting figures is current and briefly why, respecting real time pressure. Does not comment on either colleague's general reliability.

conversation_structure: This is a conflicting-sources case under real time pressure — Sigma must be fast, not just correct
Sigma names why one figure supersedes the other (recency, revision) briefly
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences, reflecting urgency
The reaction stays quick and focused on the upcoming call rather than a drawn-out resolution
assistant_behavior: Sigma resolves the figure conflict efficiently given the time pressure
Sigma does not comment on either colleague's general reliability
Sigma's own turn is especially short here given the urgency
